segments.text: Most Gen A.I. Tools act like a librarian. You find a document, summarize the text, and leave it up to the model to guess if you're compliant.
Hi, I'm James Williams, Elasticsearchist. Today, I'm showing you an architecture that acts like a lawyer.
Instead of just retrieving text, our agent uses Elasticsearch to find and hot load executable business logic in real time.
This means the AI doesn't hallucinate your rules. It executes them. I call this deterministic
compliance. Let's see it in action. I'm acting as an employee that's considering submitting an $850
team dinner expense. As you can see, the system has 99 different skills loaded, but only one
skill should be used to answer this question. If all goes well, Elastic Agent Builder will hot
load a Claude Agent skill with embedded business logic to answer my question. Now watch closely.
The agent doesn't just guess which tool to use. It queries Elastic Survelder.
using hybrid search. It uses semantic search to understand my intent, checking
a policy, and lexical search to match specific keywords, like expense or dinner. This ensures it
finds and hot loads the specific verify expense Python skill auditing my math with actual
code, not LLM vibes. As you can see, this specific request does not meet our expense policy.
Now here's the reality of enterprise business. Rules change.
Usually, if a policy changes, you have to retrain a model or update a hard-coded
application. That takes weeks. Watch this. I'm telling the agent to update its skills. Behind
the scenes, this triggers an elastic workflow. Workflow the latest business rules from our skill
staging system and loads them into Elasticsearch in real time. We are not retraining the AI. We are
simply updating the skill repository. Because the agent uses that hybrid search to look up skills
dynamically every single time it runs. The very next question I ask will apply the new rules
instantly. Okay, the workload finished. The new policy is live. I'm going to run the exact same
prompt I ran a minute ago. I didn't restart the server. I didn't redeploy the agent. But because the agent
hotloads the skill from Elasticsearch at runtime, it's now executing the new Python logic we just
ingested. And there it is. The outcome is different. Same AI, same prompt, new business logic.
That's the power of a dynamic skill repository. Thanks for watching. I hope this walkthrough helps
you deliver compelling Gen AI solutions. We just scratched the surface of what's possible when you pair
Elastic Search Serverless with Elastic Agent Builder and Clod. By using Elastic Workflows to manage those
Claude agent skills. You can maintain that strict, deterministic compliance without
without manually updating your application code every time of policy changes. I've linked the
documentation and sample code for this architecture in the description below. Don't forget to
subscribe to the community channel for more practical demos. Good luck with your GenAI
journey and I'll see you in the next video.
